observations.statement: run_with_cleanup is specified as the shared wrapper that conditionally prepares, logs and continues after prepare failure, executes the runner, invokes post-execution cleanup, and returns the execution result.

Named consumers are ExecutionEngine, research_engine, four start_chain generators, and conditionally app.rs execute_ai_turn; cleanup configuration is to come from the same run configuration used by orchestration.
PlatformRunner remains execute-only, while CleanupConfig carries untracked, ignored, agent-output, and build-artifact controls and is projected from the shared run-config shape.
Git invocation authority is centralized in shared executable resolution, with a planned transition to a dedicated git resolver while retaining one helper everywhere.

Agent scratch output has a default .puppet-master/agent-output location, optional per-run subdirectories, best-effort agent guidance, and prepare-time content clearing that preserves both the directory and current-run output until the next prepare.

Evidence retention can retain by days, by run count, or indefinitely; pruning is manual, scheduled, or background work, returns a removal count, and is intended to avoid current or in-progress evidence.

Cleanup UX includes Advanced-tab configuration for untracked, ignored, agent-output, build-artifact, and evidence controls plus a manual prepare-style clean action with confirmation for ignored cleaning or evidence pruning.

Manual cleaning must resolve the intended project from the same project/config source as a run, must not default to process CWD, and should be disabled with explanatory copy when no project context exists.
Core prepare and cleanup are internal provider-independent behavior; provider hooks, skills, plugins, extensions, and a future cleanup MCP tool are optional complements rather than dependencies.
The shortcuts surface must expose configurable bindings for text/composer input and defines thirteen default Ctrl/Alt bindings as the single default table.

Shortcut behavior includes list, edit, conflict rejection, reset, persistence, immediate key-map rebuild, defaults fallback on corrupt configuration, keyboard accessibility, and conditional platform mapping; backend wiring routes all relevant key events through the built map.

The skill model requires one SKILL.md per skill folder, enumerated frontmatter fields, six project/global discovery-path families, a constrained lowercase-hyphen name, directory-name equality, and bounded description length.

Skill loading is governed by permission.skill patterns and Persona overrides, exposed through an available-skills tool description and slash commands, automatically allowlists skill directories, and preserves skill calls through compaction.

The Skills GUI is specified to list, add, import, edit, remove or disable, permission-gate, and refresh skills; backend discovery and configuration persistence feed the UI, with explicit invalid-frontmatter and config-write failure handling.

Shortcut backend types include ShortcutAction, serializable and conflict-comparable KeyBinding values, override-only GuiConfig storage, a defaults-plus-overrides key-map builder, and startup/UI consumers of the same active map.

candidate_findings.summary: The declared wrapper-only runner contract permits a direct-execute bypass.
candidate_findings.obligation: All call sites are to use run_with_cleanup so prepare and cleanup behavior is consistent and the wrapper is the only entry point.
candidate_findings.gap: app.rs execute_ai_turn is explicitly allowed to call runner.execute directly, leaving cleanup coverage dependent on a discretionary path classification and contradicting the all-call-sites contract.

candidate_findings.summary: The process-termination cleanup capability is not reachable through the specified wrapper signature.
candidate_findings.obligation: cleanup_after_execution must attempt termination when given a positive process ID, and run_with_cleanup is the shared cleanup entry point.
candidate_findings.gap: run_with_cleanup accepts no process ID and its concrete logic always passes 0, so it cannot forward a tracked positive PID to the termination branch.

candidate_findings.summary: Execution and cleanup failure precedence is unspecified.
candidate_findings.obligation: The wrapper must execute cleanup after runner execution and return the execution result, with prepare failure explicitly treated as best-effort.
candidate_findings.gap: The contract does not state whether cleanup is guaranteed when runner.execute returns an error or is interrupted, nor whether a cleanup error is logged, returned, or allowed to replace the runner result.

candidate_findings.summary: The destructive clean-untracked default is not single-valued.
candidate_findings.obligation: Cleanup configuration is to have one shared schema and a defined default for cleaning untracked files.
candidate_findings.gap: cleanup.untracked is described as default true only when implementing Option C, while the concrete GUI element declares default true without that condition; the resulting run-time default is consequential because the action invokes git clean.

candidate_findings.summary: Evidence-pruning selection and protection rules are underdetermined.
candidate_findings.obligation: Pruning must implement day- or run-count retention while preserving current and in-progress evidence.
candidate_findings.gap: The unit called a run is deferred, precedence or combination behavior when both retention controls are set is absent, deletion may operate on both files and directories by mtime, and reference protection is conditional on feasibility with a fallback that only uses retention_days.

candidate_findings.summary: Agent-output root and lifecycle partitioning remain discretionary.
candidate_findings.obligation: Cleanup and documentation must use one shared agent-output path and the same base as prepare.
candidate_findings.gap: The path may be fixed or configurable, per-run subdirectories are optional, and the base may be work_dir or project root without a selection rule, producing different directories and clearing scope across valid implementations.

candidate_findings.obligation: The Config view is declared to remain an eight-tab surface with cleanup and evidence inside Advanced.
candidate_findings.gap: A ninth Workspace tab is simultaneously offered, and both Shortcuts and Skills may independently become dedicated tabs, without a rule reconciling those choices with the eight-tab requirement.

candidate_findings.summary: Reset-all is both optional and required.
candidate_findings.obligation: Shortcut acceptance requires the user to reset one action or reset all actions to defaults and rebuild the persisted key map.
candidate_findings.gap: The GUI behavior section labels Reset all to defaults optional, leaving two incompatible capability sets.

candidate_findings.summary: Platform shortcut normalization lacks a canonical persistence boundary.
candidate_findings.obligation: Platform-appropriate shortcuts must be displayed and stored through one DRY mapping while the active key map is persisted and rebuilt.
candidate_findings.gap: Support is conditional and mapping may occur when reading, writing, or displaying configuration, so the capsule does not establish whether stored overrides are canonical Ctrl/Alt values or platform-translated Cmd/Option values.

candidate_findings.summary: First-wins skill discovery lacks an exact ordering and identity contract in this capsule.
candidate_findings.obligation: The GUI list must reflect ordered discovery paths and first-wins deduplication.
candidate_findings.gap: The paths are grouped and walking from cwd to the worktree is required, but nearest-first versus root-first traversal and the deduplication key are not defined here; refresh behavior delegates to an ordered-path contract outside this window.

candidate_findings.summary: Skill import and removal have divergent mutation semantics.
candidate_findings.obligation: Users must be able to import and remove skills, with confirmation before deletion.
candidate_findings.gap: Import may create or link, while removal may delete a folder or merely hide it through permissions; the plan does not select a behavior or define link ownership, disable persistence, or when the acceptance-level Remove action performs deletion.

candidate_findings.summary: Resolved skill-permission precedence is not specified in the capsule.
candidate_findings.obligation: The GUI must render a resolved permission from per-skill or wildcard patterns while Persona profiles may further restrict or allow skills.
candidate_findings.gap: No precedence rule is given for overlapping patterns or for combining GuiConfig skill permissions with Persona overrides, despite the list requiring one resolved permission per skill.

candidate_findings.summary: Missing-SKILL.md state has two incompatible GUI truths.
candidate_findings.obligation: Missing SKILL.md failures must surface clearly without corrupting state.
candidate_findings.gap: Discovery may either omit the directory completely or display an invalid entry, changing list contents and user remediation with no selected behavior.

candidate_findings.summary: Several declared Skills capabilities have no behavior contract.
candidate_findings.obligation: Sort, filter, preview, and validate-all are listed among the features that must live in the Skills location.
candidate_findings.gap: Those capabilities have no defined inputs, state transitions, outputs, failure behavior, or acceptance criteria, and they are absent from the implementation checklist.

candidate_findings.summary: Behavioral acceptance outcomes lack specified evidence production.
candidate_findings.obligation: Shortcut and Skills screens have explicit user-visible acceptance outcomes.
candidate_findings.gap: The checklists name widget-catalog generation and reuse checks but do not identify tests, fixtures, receipts, or manual evidence for shortcut persistence and immediate activation, discovery ordering, mutations, permissions, or error paths.

candidate_findings.summary: Cross-plan cleanup and Source Control correctness obligations are not executable contracts.
candidate_findings.obligation: Cleanup and worktree visibility must cover named orchestration objects and Source Control lineage requirements.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule lists work packages, feature seams, project summaries, controls, filtering, partitioning, hostability, lane binding, and lineage as correctness requirements without defining their states, consumers, data flow, or acceptance evidence.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Prepare failure handling is explicit: log the error and continue as best-effort.
Cleanup and evidence fields are explicitly required to share the application's existing configuration schema rather than creating a cleanup-only configuration source.
Agent-output clearing is explicitly limited to prepare time, preserves current-run output until the next prepare, and removes contents rather than the directory itself.
Until an evidence-retention policy is active, the explicit default is to retain all evidence.
Manual clean has an explicit directory-safety rule: derive the project root from run-equivalent context, never incidental CWD, and disable the action when context is absent.
Provider hooks and plugins are explicitly non-authoritative for core cleanup; internal prepare and cleanup remain required.
The complete default shortcut action-to-key table is explicitly enumerated.
Duplicate shortcut handling and corrupt-config handling are explicit: reject the conflicting update without changing config, and fall back to defaults with user-visible notification on load failure.
Shortcut changes explicitly rebuild the same active key map immediately after persistence, and GUI key handling must use configured bindings rather than hardcoded bindings.
Skill discovery-path families and name, directory-match, and description validation constraints are explicit.
Deleting a skill folder without explicit confirmation is prohibited.
Skill-list refresh timing is explicit and excludes timer-based automatic refresh.
Invalid frontmatter must not overwrite the skill file, and permission-write failure must preserve in-memory edits for retry.

unknowns.statement: Whether macOS support is in scope is unknown.
unknowns.reason: Both platform-appropriate storage/display and Ctrl-to-Cmd mapping are conditional on supporting macOS.

unknowns.statement: The canonical Config locations for Shortcuts and Skills are unresolved.
unknowns.reason: Each surface permits multiple tab, subsection, or Settings placements, and the Skills location is still expressed as alternatives.

unknowns.statement: The exact unit and authoritative state used by retain_last_runs are unknown.
unknowns.reason: The configuration text defers defining a run, and protection of referenced current runs is conditional on feasibility.

unknowns.statement: Behavior for a provider that does not support skill loading is unknown.
unknowns.reason: Allowed skills are passed only for platforms that support skills, with no fallback or user-visible unsupported state specified here.

unknowns.statement: The winning project-root source when several project and config hints are simultaneously available is unknown.
unknowns.reason: The contract offers current project, config-path parent, and configured working-directory sources but gives no precedence among them beyond requiring consistency with the run.
